brief: A sole-trader plumber in Stockport fixing failed boilers, leaks and bathrooms for homeowners and landlords across the borough.

sources.note: My boiler stopped working on a Sunday and I needed someone I could trust in my house quickly. He gave a fixed price on the phone and sent a photo of the finished pipework. I want to know who is coming to my house and see the actual work. I am a landlord and my tenant had no heating.
The van is bottle green with white hand-painted capitals and a plain outline border.
sources.lettering: Hand-painted capitals with a plain outline border.

sources.note: Photographs taken on a phone of finished boiler and pipework jobs, each with the street and date written on a card in the shot.
Tom Aldous works alone, answers his own phone and is on the Gas Safe register under his own name.

statement.object: a plumber they can trust in their house to fix a failed boiler
statement.context: quickly, without being overcharged by someone they have never met

functional.value: Their boiler stopped working and they need someone to fix it quickly.

emotional.value: They worry about letting a stranger into their house and being overcharged.

social.value: A landlord needs to show the tenant who had no heating that it was fixed properly.

consideration.because: The boiler stopped working on a Sunday, so the choice is made within minutes of searching.

objections: letting a stranger into my house
language: I needed someone I could trust in my house quickly
I want to know who is coming to my house

primaryAction.because: The low consideration job is a stopped boiler, so a visitor wants to ring at once, and the call stays pinned while they check who is coming.

order.because: A stopped boiler needs someone quickly, so Tom's name, the van and one finished boiler job come first.
The visitor wants to see the actual work before letting a stranger into the house, so the work follows.
Landlords and homeowners say they trusted him in their house, so their words come after the work.
The failed boiler is the urgent job, so the services list comes once trust is established.
A visitor who has seen who is coming and the work can ring without scrolling back up.

lead.value: Failed boilers fixed by Tom himself
lead.because: A stopped boiler is the urgent job, and the visitor wants the same man who answers the phone to be the one who comes.

journey.because: A visitor with a stopped boiler first needs to see this is a plumber who covers their street.
Before letting a stranger into the house, the visitor wants to know who is coming and see the work.
Once they know who is coming, a quick call gets the boiler fixed without being overcharged on the day.

proof.what: one photograph of a finished boiler job with the street and date on a card in the shot
proof.because: The visitor wants to see the actual work before letting a stranger into the house, so one finished job is met on the first screen.

proof.what: Tom's name, the van and a line saying he answers the phone himself
proof.because: The visitor asks who is coming to the house, and the name and the van answer it on the first screen without a portrait.

proof.what: every job photograph with a caption saying what was fixed
proof.because: Captions about each boiler job are detail for a visitor who wants more, so they sit in the work section and not in the way.

proof.what: three customer quotes about trusting him in the house
proof.because: Customers describing trusting a stranger in their house answers the visitor's own worry in the words of someone who did.

accent.because: The hand-painted capitals on the van set its colour, so the same colour marks the call button.

ground.because: The van's white panels sit behind its green lettering, so the page ground follows them.

display.because: The hand-painted capitals on the van are sturdy and squared, which a slab headline echoes.

body.because: The plain outline lettering on the van keeps supporting text simple and easy to read.

shape.because: The plain outline border on the van has square corners, so the buttons keep them.
